issues.legal_issue: A commitment to trial for criminal conspiracy cannot stand where the evidence does not provide a prima facie basis to infer the accused’s knowledge of the fraudulent claim or prior concert with the other accused.
material_facts: The accused was a lawyer who filed applications and vakalatnamas for the other accused and identified them as claimants to compensation.
The documentary evidence did not show that the lawyer knew the other accused were not the rightful claimants or that he had agreed with them before filing the applications.
The prosecution relied on the lawyer’s identification of the claimants and his fee, but the Court did not regard either circumstance as incriminating evidence of conspiracy.

The lawyer had accepted responsibility to refund the money in case of wrongful payment, sought a voucher in his own name for a genuine claimant, and deposited part of the money in that claimant’s bank account.
issues.conclusion: There was no prima facie evidence supporting the conspiracy charge against the lawyer, so the commitment order against him was quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code, the evidence must provide a prima facie basis for the conspiracy charge. Under Raj Pal v. Jai Singh, a magistrate should not commit an accused to the Court of Session when there is no prima facie evidence or when the evidence is entirely unworthy of credit. Here, representing and identifying purported claimants, without evidence of prior knowledge or concert, did not provide that basis; the cited circumstantial matters did not alter the result.

rule.if: sessions_commitment_for_conspiracy and lawyer_represented_claimants and no_evidence_of_prior_concert and no_evidence_of_knowledge_of_false_claim and identification_and_fee_are_only_incriminating_circumstances and conduct_supports_bona_fides

predicates.sessions_commitment_for_conspiracy: The proceeding is a commitment to the Court of Session on a criminal conspiracy charge.
predicates.lawyer_represented_claimants: The accused acted as a lawyer for persons claiming an entitlement to the disputed payment and identified them as claimants.
predicates.no_evidence_of_prior_concert: The prosecution evidence did not show that the accused and the purported claimants had agreed together before the lawyer filed the applications.
predicates.no_evidence_of_knowledge_of_false_claim: The prosecution evidence did not show that the lawyer knew the purported claimants were not entitled to the payment.
predicates.identification_and_fee_are_only_incrimin: The prosecution relied on the lawyer’s role in identifying the claimants and the fee he received, without other incriminating circumstances establishing his participation in a conspiracy.
predicates.conduct_supports_bona_fides: The lawyer accepted responsibility for refunding a wrongful payment and handled part of the money in a way consistent with payment to a genuine claimant.
predicates.commitment_quashed: The commitment to trial on the conspiracy charge is set aside.

issues.definition: When a lawyer is committed for conspiracy after representing purported claimants, the commitment is quashed if the evidence shows no prior concert or knowledge of a false claim and the identified incriminating circumstances are insufficient in light of conduct supporting bona fides.
